text.en: The Beggar's Opera (London, 1728) set new words to tunes everyone already knew, such as "Over the Hills and far away" and "Green Sleeves".

source.en: Gay, The Beggar's Opera (the 1765 edition's airs)

headline.en: In a show, a song is the moment speaking isn't enough. Buttercup is selling her wares to a ship full of sailors: say her line, then sing it.

headline.en: A breath belongs at the end of a thought, not at every comma. Breathing mid-thought cuts the sense in two.

text.en: Sullivan said the first thing he decided in a song was its rhythm: "I arrange the rhythm before I come to the question of melody."

headline.en: Why, I, my, day: each is two vowels. Hold the first, and give the second only at the very end. On high notes vowels bend; down here, keep them true.

headline.en: Ko-Ko spins a sad tale of a little bird to win Katisha's heart. The time is 6/8: feel it in two big beats, not six small ones.

headline.en: The button is a song's last note, held to its value, stopped on the beat, then stillness while the thought lands.

text.en: "Sweet Little Buttercup I", the "I" held and stopped on the beat.

questions.en: Did you stay still and keep the thought for a moment after the note?
Did the last note stay steady to its end?
